solidity:solidity.why: SOL-15. The floor moved UP, which is the direction that normally means a regression, so the reason is recorded rather than the number quietly edited. Two repairs landed together. (1) The analyzer's `revert_statement` case had NEVER FIRED — it tested `namedChild(0).type === "identifier"` and the grammar puts an `expression` wrapper there for every spelling — so 453 custom-error call edges over the 389-file corpus did not exist in this lane at all. (2) The ORACLE had the identical dead branch, which is why F5 agreed at zero: two instruments that are both dead look like corroboration. Fixing only the analyzer made the pair disagree and F5 reported 37 unexplained edges that no re-run would clear, because `sweepStateKey` hashed every analyzer in src/ast but NOT script/m14/oracles — so an oracle edit left the journal key byte-identical and the next run printed `RESUMED` with the previous truth function's numbers. All three are fixed: the oracles are now part of the sweep state. On the adjudication draw the oracle repair cut calls-unexplained from 47 to 2. The residual 3 is custom-error calls to an error declared in ANOTHER file, classified `evm-member-call` alongside the rest of the cross-file residue; `unclassifiable` is 0.

julia:julia.why: First floor for the julia lane, recorded from a real F5 probe rather than declared. The sample ROTATES 60 of 941 files per run, so `missing` and `unexplained` move between runs on the same code — observed 98.5%/8.5%, 99.3%/9.6% and 98.0%/9.6% across three probes this session. The stable figures are the unexplained RATE and a direct 40-file measurement (extends 39/39, instantiates 27/27, uses 98.8%, references 97.3%), so the floor is set from the WEAKEST probe rather than the best, and the reason is recorded here because a floor that moves silently is indistinguishable from a regression being tolerated.
julia:julia.note: unexplained is dominated by the oracles' own scope limits — they decline cross-file callee resolution — plus @eval module and quoted-block shapes. Widening them would mean guessing.
